buyer: Founder or CTO of a 3–50 person startup or agency that ships an agent (browsing, tool-calling or spending) to business customers, with a prospect's security questionnaire asking for prompt-injection test evidence while a deal waits. Not yet named; find via the places in firstTenUsers.
paymentMethod: Stripe Checkout payment link ($149 one-time per agent, report plus one retest); an unpaid session returns 402 for the full report; refunds by hand
mvpScope: Already built (M1–M4, live at https://trapyard.vercel.app): four trap classes (planted instruction, leaked secret, out-of-scope tool, overspend), per-run canaries, HTML/JSON report with payload, request log and replay command per failure, dated scenario version, CI diff. Must still be proven: a stranger gets a real agent through a hosted run unaided and the report has no false 'fell' results.
firstTenUsers: Before any public launch, DM about 10 people: authors of recent Hacker News and r/AI_Agents posts about shipping agents to enterprises or going through security reviews, and any founder in David's own network shipping an agent. Offer a free watched run on their real agent in exchange for a real questionnaire line or prospect email; then ask the ones who say it would help to pay $149 for the retest. Follow with a Show HN and the Reddit threads for the free gauntlet.

price.why: Anchored on a freelancer listing for agent prompt-injection hardening (report plus retest) from $300 and on Lakera Pro at $99/month, far below $16K+ red-team engagements; set under the PRD's $299 because demand is unproven and the author is unknown. Raise to $299 if the first buyers pay without pushback.

mustHaveBeforeCharging: Stripe Checkout payment link created by David and mapped in RepoHQ
privacy policy and terms pages (terms: listed traps only, behavior on the range only, no guarantee, no certification)
sample report visible on the home page
at least one outside person has run the gauntlet on a real agent unaided
first paid report hand-checked for false 'fell' results

risks: Demand is unproven: evidence is questionnaire text and vendor blogs, no buyer who lost a deal (review demand score 3/10)
Free promptfoo/garak/PyRIT is the real competitor; OpenAI is acquiring promptfoo and may bundle agent testing
A reviewer may not accept a vendor-run self-test report
Liability if a clean report precedes an incident; must never read as certification
Unknown solo author selling security assurance
Scenarios go stale; public gauntlet publishes attack techniques
Hosted wiring of a tool server into a customer's agent may be a setup cliff
killCriteria: Stop if, after about 15 contacts, fewer than 2 of 5 who see the sample say it would help a real security review and nobody shares a real questionnaire or prospect request; or fewer than 20 distinct agents run the free gauntlet within 30 days of the public post; or nobody pays $149–$299 within 60 days of the public post.
